intro.text: Ryder System, Inc. (Ryder) is a leading provider of outsourced logistics and transportation services throughout North America. We offer port‑to‑door solutions that integrate every step of the supply chain, including international inbound flows and cross‑border logistics, fleet and transportation management, warehousing, manufacturing support and multi-channel final delivery. Our complementary business segments provide a broad range of value-added solutions, which provides our customers with a seamless, end‑to‑end logistics network designed to reduce complexity and improve speed, reliability and efficiency across the entire flow of goods. Ryder connects every link in the supply chain, moving products smoothly from ports and suppliers all the way to customers’ doorsteps as illustrated below.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In 2025, our global FMS business accounted for 38% of our consolidated revenue.
During 2025, ChoiceLease revenue accounted for 60% of our FMS total revenue.
During 2025, commercial rental revenue accounted for 16% of our FMS total revenue.
During 2025, SelectCare revenue accounted for 12% of our FMS total revenue.
During 2025, fuel services revenue accounted for 12% of our FMS total revenue.
During 2025, our SCS business accounted for 43% of our consolidated revenue, and our customer accounts and warehousing square footage were as follows:
During 2025, distribution management and value-added services accounted for approximately 36% of our SCS total revenue.
During 2025, transportation management solutions accounted for 12% of our SCS total revenue.
During 2025, our e-commerce and last mile services accounted for 18% of our SCS total revenue.
During 2025, our contract manufacturing and contract packaging services and other services accounted for 6% of our SCS total revenue.
During 2025, our DTS business accounted for 18% of our consolidated revenue.
(1) During 2025, 2024 and 2023, rental revenue from lease customers in place of a lease vehicle represented 29%, 31%, and 34% of commercial rental revenue, respectively.
Our business relies on the strength of our customers' businesses and their level of confidence in current and future economic conditions.
Overall, the extent to which future supply chain disruptions impact our business, operations and financial results will depend on numerous factors that are difficult to accurately predict.
Our success depends on the functionality of information technology systems to support our business and service offerings.
We depend on the integrity of our information and the proper functioning and availability of our information systems in operating our business.
We and the vehicle equipment manufacturers in our FMS business rely on a small number of suppliers.
Some of our OEMs rely on a small concentration of suppliers for certain vehicle parts, components and equipment.

Although we believe we have alternative sources of supply for the equipment and other supplies used in our business, termination or significant alteration of our relationship with any of our key suppliers could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition or results of operations in the unlikely event that we were unable to obtain adequate equipment or supplies from other sources in a timely manner or at all.
Our principal sources of financing are issuances of unsecured commercial paper and medium-term notes.
A significant downgrade below investment grade of our short-term debt ratings would impair our ability to issue commercial paper and likely require us to rely on alternative funding sources.
In making our assessments of fair value, we rely on our knowledge and experience about past and current events and assumptions about conditions we expect to exist in the future.

Our SCS and DTS services provided within a contract depend on a significant level of integration and interdependency between the services and are generally considered integrated arrangements with revenue recognized as the interdependent services are delivered.
